title: Affine etale neighbourhood of the image of a quasi-compact scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $C$ be a quasi-compact $S$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] with an $S$-morphism $c:C\to E$. There exist an affine $S$-scheme $U$ and a representable etale morphism $u:h_U\to E$ such that the scheme projection $V=C\times_EU\to C$ is surjective, etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Here affine means isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$, and the fibre product is the sheaf fibre product represented by a scheme, as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Neither $E$ nor $S$ is assumed separated or quasi-compact, and $V\to C$ is not asserted quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, proof paragraph choosing the affine etale U above the quasi-compact image; Tags 03FX (lemma-cover-by-union-affines), 03BX (lemma-topology-points), and 03FZ (lemma-separated-cover). Local quasi-finiteness of the etale scheme projection is Morphisms Tag 03WS, lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite, in morphisms.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] to obtain a scheme $W=\coprod_{i\in I}W_i$ with every $W_i$ affine and a representable surjective etale map $w:h_W\to E$ with $|w|$ surjective. Write $\iota_i:W_i\to W$ for the coprojections of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; they are open immersions with disjoint images covering $W$, so $O_i=|w|(\iota_i(W_i))$ is the image of the open set $\iota_i(W_i)$ under the open map $|w|$ (openness clause of [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]) and the $O_i$ are open sets covering $|E|$. By the continuity clause of the same node, $|c|:|C|\to|E|$ is continuous, so the sets $|c|^{-1}(O_i)$ form an open covering of $C$. Since $C$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], there is a finite set $J\subseteq I$ with $C=\bigcup_{j\in J}|c|^{-1}(O_j)$ ($J=\varnothing$ if $C$ is empty). Let $U\subseteq W$ be the open subscheme $\bigcup_{j\in J}\iota_j(W_j)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] it is the coproduct $\coprod_{j\in J}W_j$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] it is affine, isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\prod_{j\in J}A_j$ where $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ (for $J=\varnothing$ this is the empty scheme $\operatorname{Spec}0$). Let $u=w\circ k$ where $k:U\to W$ is the open immersion; it is an $S$-morphism. It is representable etale: for a scheme $T$ with $h_T\to E$, the sheaf $h_T\times_Eh_U$ equals $(h_T\times_Eh_W)\times_{h_W}h_U$; by [def-trf-algebraic-space] $P=h_T\times_Eh_W$ is a scheme etale over $T$, and $P\times_WU$ is the open subscheme of $P$ lying over $U$ (the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of a scheme with an open immersion is the open preimage, checked on the universal property). An open immersion is etale and composites of etale morphisms are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2), so $P\times_WU\to T$ is etale. Finally the image of $|u|$ is $\bigcup_{j\in J}O_j$, which contains $|c|(|C|)$.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, proof paragraph choosing the affine etale U; inputs Tags 03FX (lemma-cover-by-union-affines), 03BX (lemma-topology-points), 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), and the finite coproduct construction.

proof.text: Form the sheaf fibre product $V=C\times_EU$. By the definition of representable etale maps in [def-trf-algebraic-space], applied to $u$ and the scheme $C$, $V$ is a scheme and $V\to C$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For every point $x\in C$, step 1 gives a point $y\in|U|$ with $|u|(y)=|c|(x)$; [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] then gives a point of $V$ mapping to $x$. Hence $V\to C$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proof paragraph defining $V=U\times_{X,c}T\prime$ and asserting representability, etaleness and surjectivity; Tags 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian) and 03BX (lemma-topology-points).

proof.text: The affine scheme $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ is separated: its diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the surjective multiplication map $B\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B\to B$, hence a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism] (Stacks 01KN; elementary). So [lem-a1-separated-etale-chart] applies to the representable etale chart $u$ and the scheme $C$ with $c$: its second clause says exactly that $V=C\times_EU\to C$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 03FZ (lemma-separated-cover), together with Morphisms Tag 01UA for base-change permanence of separatedness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite] to the algebraic space $h_V$ (a scheme, hence an algebraic space by [def-trf-algebraic-space]) with $f:h_V\to C$ the projection of step 2, and target the scheme $C$. Its chartwise hypothesis holds: if $v:h_{V'}\to h_V$ is representable etale with $V'$ a scheme, then the base change of $v$ along $\mathrm{id}_V$ is $V'\to V$ itself, so $V'\to V$ is etale by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $V'\to V\to C$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2), since $V\to C$ is etale by step 2. Its conclusion for the chart $v=\mathrm{id}_V$ says that $V\to C$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. With steps 2 and 3 this gives all four asserted properties.

split_report.summary: Split the affine-chart paragraph of Gabber's Tag 0APL proof. The first step uses the existing affine etale cover of an algebraic space, openness of etale maps, quasi-compactness, and finite affine coproducts to choose one affine chart whose image contains c(C). The second step uses the pointwise fibre-product criterion and etale base change to prove that V is a surjective etale scheme over C. The separatedness input is isolated in a statement-only chart lemma, and the existing algebraic-space etale-to-locally-quasi-finite lemma supplies local quasi-finiteness. The statement and all hypotheses are unchanged.
